Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Read the Active section of .agent-work/LESSONS.md if it exists: these are distilled workflow lessons from prior runs — condition planning and handoff authoring on them, and note any lesson this run's evidence contradicts (it becomes a disconfirm op at the feedback step). Read the current map (packets, overlays, decision anchors) for the area the ask touches; this read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. The checklist config_ref (docs/agents/engine-config.json) is absent-by-design in repos that vendor their own scripts (a skill-source repo has no docs/agents/ overlay at all); the engine degrades it gracefully to built-in defaults (rework cap, lease-stale seconds), so a missing engine-config is a sanctioned degradation, not a gap to fix — do NOT create the overlay file. If a run in such a repo needs non-default engine settings, inline a `config` object on the checklist (the engine prefers an inline `config` over `config_ref`) rather than chasing the dead path. Attest c1.

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the current map using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope (attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); bare 'none' entries fail the invariant check. Append one dated entry for this work-id to .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md (create it from templates/AGENT_FEEDBACK.template.md if absent — prefer the project copy under .agent-work/templates/, fall back to the bundled workbench template). This log persists across runs and is never archived with the work-id. Adjudicate each lesson before banking it — the playbook holds open problems you are carrying forward, not a log of everything learned. If a lesson is understood and fixable now, APPLY it this run (make the bounded edit, record it in AGENT_FEEDBACK) and do not add a playbook entry at all; a lesson goes in the bank (an add) ONLY because it needs to be re-observed to be understood, and every add must carry a bank_reason saying what re-observation will clarify. Applying to project doctrine (a docs/agents/* delta or a template working copy — any .md / .template.*) is a human call: it needs authority=human on the apply op, and in delegated/autonomous mode you do NOT self-apply doctrine — surface it to your principal (who may rule 'apply', or 'wait, observe it again') and defer with 'needs human' until they do. Applying a code target (with its test suite as proof) stays autonomous. Then distill what remains into the playbook: write structured delta ops (add [with bank_reason]/confirm/disconfirm/mention/retire/apply/defer — every add/confirm/disconfirm cites a grounding artifact line; corroborate with engine telemetry like rework counts, BLOCK verdicts, waives where possible) to .agent-work/300/lessons-delta.json with tick=true, and apply deterministically: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py .agent-work/300/lessons-delta.json --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md. Never edit LESSONS.md directly; if there are no lesson candidates, still apply a tick-only delta. Then settle every threshold-ripe lesson (python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py --ripe --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md): for each, APPLY it (make the bounded edit to its target — a thin docs/agents/* delta or a project template working copy — confirmed by the human, then an apply op deletes it as paid), or for a constellation lesson EXPORT it (append to .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md — carry the originating lesson id in that entry's Lesson field so the upstream sweep groups recurrences on stable identity, rewording a recurring finding via amend not a new slug — then an export op marks it exported and pinned), or RESOLVE it if you can confirm the upstream fix has already shipped (a resolve op citing the shipping PR/commit marks the constellation lesson fixed-upstream: no longer ripe, immune to re-confirmation, and it ages out of the playbook — this is how an already-fixed defect stops being re-exported every run), or DEFER it with a reason (a broad or contradictory doctrine shift routes to a Charter refresh; an autonomous run without that latitude defers 'needs human'). Lessons flagged charter-review go to a Charter refresh. Then run the feedback invariant check before advancing: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py 300 --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including the appended .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md entry — where the repo tracks .agent-work/. Where .agent-work/ is gitignored, do not try to commit it: the durable copy is the work-area-root AGENT_FEEDBACK.md file itself, uncommitted; when this run is dispatched under an Admiral, the epic-level harvest at closeout is the durable record instead. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/300/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-300/, leaving the unified AGENT_FEEDBACK.md at the agent-work root. Run the archive-phase feedback invariant check before marking archive complete: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py 300 --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): <engine> release --session-id commander-300. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.
